neighbours.label: ' a' / ' an' and the adjective after it, when a general or abstract qualifier follows 'with' or 'as well as' (with an increased risk, as well as a general lack); the indefinite article before concrete objects stays quiet
fire: Smoking is linked to heart disease, with an increased risk of stroke.
Poor roads, as well as a general lack of funding, slowed the work.
The region faced a dry decade, with a widespread loss of crops.
Her illness came with a marked decline in appetite.
The project has limited staff, as well as a growing shortage of parts.
Farmers ended the year with a modest rise in income.
Cities grew quickly, with an overall drop in rural population.
Bad weather, as well as a sudden fall in demand, hurt the port.
quiet: Smoking was banned at the depot, where a man sold an apple.
Old roads ran past a barn and a small red shed.
The region built a dam and a canal across the valley.
Her uncle came with a bag and a loaf of bread.
The project has a van and an office near the station.
Farmers ended the day at a table with a jug of beer.
Cities grew quickly, and an old tram ran to a park.
A truck and a bus were parked at the port.
